findings.desc: delivery-check-hash.ts:94 advisory field is optional on DeliveryCheckFreshnessResult but is semantically required when code===delivery_check_drift_advisory; missing discriminated union means a future code path returning that code without advisory would silently swallow the advisory (done-oracle uses the defensive ? empty-string guard at line 629). The type should enforce advisory presence for the advisory code.

CHK-001:happy:2 must-intent (delivery_waiver_add re-sign preserves storyFilesHash) has no dynamic execution evidence: the smoke never calls delivery_waiver_add, and the evidence note explicitly admits this ("The smoke test ... does not have an explicit waiver case"). The submitted evidence is kind=logic_test + a grep command that confirms the field is referenced in source, but this cannot catch a runtime defect such as reading an old-format record that lacks storyFilesHash and silently passing undefined to re-sign. A must-priority cli-type intent requires either a smoke/integration_test call exercising the actual waiver path or a waiver with a clear rationale for why automation is impractical.

CHK-001:edge:1, CHK-002:edge:1, CHK-002:adversarial:2, CHK-003:edge:1: evidence kind=logic_test but command= node packages/main/dist/tasks/delivery-check-freshness-smoke.js. The kind field declares this is a logic (static code) inspection, but the command field points to the smoke binary. A reviewer cannot determine from the evidence record whether the claim is backed by a live smoke execution (which would be manual_transcript) or a code-reading argument (which should have a grep/cat command, not the smoke binary). This ambiguity undermines auditability: if the smoke were to regress, these entries would still record kind=logic_test and could be mistaken for independent static proof rather than smoke-dependent evidence.

CHK-003:happy:1 intent: normal fresh delivery-check -> DONE row passes with NO advisory appended. The smoke case (delivery-check-freshness-smoke.ts:212-244) asserts row.status=pass but does not assert that row.detail does NOT contain the advisory string. The evidence note explains the absence via code reasoning (done-oracle.ts only appends advisorySuffix when freshness.advisory is truthy), but there is no pinned assert.doesNotMatch(row.detail, /ADVISORY/) assertion in the smoke. If done-oracle.ts were accidentally changed to always append some advisory text, the CHK-003:happy:1 smoke case would still pass. Advisory suppression on the fresh path is a behavioral invariant worth pinning explicitly.
